findings.reason: without a control that duplicates the synthesis's own rendered section, one of the seven assertions the gate is graded on is never shown to be able to fail.
findings.text: seven cases are graded by six negative controls: rendering only the synthesis's own sections drops x-appended (case 1), carrying every section carries s9 (case 3), ignoring unmarked sections drops legacy-anchor (case 4), exempting marked sections duplicates (case 5), accepting any anchor stores (case 6), dropping silently unnames (case 7), and no control falsifies case 2

findings.reason: the deliverable's promise that a published anchor keeps resolving and that no append is dropped silently is false for that pre-marker class, so the plan should either name those drops in the result or state the limitation explicitly.
findings.text: the legacy rule ("an unmarked section counts as appended when its id is none of the ids a synthesis can produce") classifies a pre-marker append anchored to a plan section id or to an id the synthesis now renders as NOT appended, so it is dropped as a stale generated section and is excluded from the result's dropped-anchor field the plan says names every dropped append
